title: Change
content: It's the placement season and honestly it startles me a bit considering the fact that there's less than 6 months left of our college...of our educational journey and I am this close to achieving my long held wish... the wish I held since I started this journey... the wish to be finally free from the never ending and endless repeating cycle of studying, exams and results but now that I am so close, it all seems a blip in time. I have already lived 21 years or 1,83,960 hours (thank you god) and I have spent more than half of this vast expanses of time (almost the entire lifespan of a cat) studying and the funny thing is, I don't even remember most of the things I learnt (except that mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell), so does that mean I spent all of that time for nothing? well as someone said "sometimes the journey is more beautiful than the destination" so yeah, I don't remember most of the things I sacrificed my nights learning and even if I did I am pretty sure it won't be of any help to me in the next journey of my life but all that wasn't in vain since it certainly did taught me the joy of pursuing a goal no matter how small and the the even greater joy of finally achieving it. In a way, it prepared me for the next stage of my life and taught me that as humans WE WISH FOR A CHANGE WHILE BEING AFRAID OF IT.

title: Gods in some shops, gurus in others
excerpt: Walking past shops today I noticed something.
observation: Walking past shops today I noticed something. Most shops had idols of gods, but in Baniya shops it was mostly a photo of their guru. Same street, same kind of shop, different face on the wall. Why?
question: Why do Baniya shops keep a guru photo instead of a god?
answer: Old trade in India ran on trust, not contracts. Marwari and Gujarati traders moved money across the country with hundis, basically paper IOUs, and gave credit on a handshake. That only works if you can trust the other person, and the cheapest way to trust someone was knowing they are from your community. Cheat someone and the whole community hears about it: your standing, your marriages, your business, gone. A shared guru is the shortcut to ONE OF US. Same guru means same satsangs, same gatherings, same values, like no alcohol or being vegetarian. So that photo quietly tells other traders and suppliers you belong to their circle and follow the same rules, which means easier credit, referrals and repeat customers. It even tells walk-in buyers this shop runs on values. Honest caveat: most shopkeepers put it up out of genuine devotion, not strategy. The signal is a side effect. But it is a side effect that kept trading communities strong for centuries.

title: Chot
observation: I had this chot (scrape) on my foot from a few days back, and today I finally peeled off the scab, a big one. The second it came off, it took me straight back to childhood, when I used to get a new chot almost every single week. It's been so long since I've had one like this.
question: Why did I stop getting hurt like this?
answer: Because I stopped playing like that. As a kid I was outside constantly, running and cycling around with my friends, getting scraped up without even noticing. Growing up just quietly took that away, replaced it with other things to be busy with. I don't miss the chot. I miss the playing that used to cause it.
